evals.prompt: I'm building an AI agent in Go using Google's ADK. I want it to: 1) take a city name and call a custom tool to fetch the weather (mock data is fine), then 2) have a second agent summarize that weather report in a friendly tone. Wire it up as a sequential pipeline and show me how to run it with an in-memory runner. Save it as main.go.
evals.expected_output: A main.go using google.golang.org/adk/v2 with a functiontool-based weather tool, two llmagent agents chained via OutputKey/{placeholder}, wired into a sequentialagent pipeline, run via a runner.
expectations: Imports use the google.golang.org/adk/v2/... path prefix (not the un-versioned google.golang.org/adk/... v1 path)
A custom weather tool is defined via functiontool.New with a typed args struct and a handler taking agent.Context (not the v1 tool.Context alias)
Two llmagent.New agents are created: one that calls the weather tool, one that summarizes in a friendly tone, connected via OutputKey and a {placeholder} in the second agent's Instruction
The two agents are wired into a sequentialagent.New pipeline (or otherwise run in a fixed sequential order)
The code runs the pipeline via a runner (either runner.New + runner.Config, or the v2 runner.NewInMemory convenience constructor) and iterates the returned events
The model is constructed via gemini.NewModel with a plausible current model id (e.g. gemini-flash-latest), not a clearly fictional or deprecated-looking id
No output claims the code was actually executed or verified

evals.prompt: Using ADK Go, build a refund-processing workflow with the graph-based orchestration engine: validate the refund request, check the refund policy, and if the amount is over $500, pause the whole workflow and wait for a human approver before issuing the refund. It needs to be able to survive a process restart while waiting for approval. Save the code to refund_workflow.go.
evals.expected_output: Go code using google.golang.org/adk/v2/workflow with distinct validate/policy-check/approval/issue nodes, conditional routing on the $500 threshold, and durable HITL (ResumeOrRequestInput / RequestInput) rather than an in-memory wait.
expectations: Uses the google.golang.org/adk/v2/workflow graph engine package, not just sequentialagent/parallelagent/loopagent, for the branching/pause logic
Includes distinct steps/nodes for validating the request and checking refund policy before any approval or issuance step
Implements the >$500 branch using conditional/dynamic routing (e.g. a DynamicNode with RunNode, or workflow routing helpers), not a hardcoded unconditional path

Uses the durable HITL primitive (workflow.ResumeOrRequestInput and/or workflow.NewRequestInputEvent with session.RequestInput) for the human-approval pause, not just an in-memory channel/sleep/blocking wait
Demonstrates or explicitly describes a resume path needed to satisfy 'survive a process restart' (loading the session and re-invoking the graph with the human's answer), not just the initial pause
Does not conflate this graph-level pause with the separate, per-tool-call tool.WithConfirmation mechanism as if they were the same thing
The refund issuance step only runs after the approval gate for amounts over $500, not unconditionally

wf.Run (or the mechanism used to start the graph) is invoked with an agent.InvocationContext, typically by driving the *Workflow through a runner rather than calling wf.Run directly with a bare context.Context

The resume path is implemented by calling runner.Run again with a message that answers the pending interrupt (e.g. a genai.Content carrying a FunctionResponse keyed to the InterruptID), not by calling wf.Resume directly with a hand-built context.Context or agent.Context

evals.expected_output: Correctly identifies the /v2 import path change, the ToolContext/CallbackContext merge into agent.Context, the resulting mock-compilation break, and recommends agent.StrictContextMock (or lists the concrete missing methods) — with corrected code.
expectations: States the module import path must change from google.golang.org/adk/... to google.golang.org/adk/v2/...
States that tool.Context should become agent.Context (the unified context type), not just a mechanical find-replace with no explanation
States that agent.CallbackContext no longer exists as a separate type and is merged into agent.Context, and explains the mock-compilation impact this has
Recommends or shows agent.StrictContextMock as the preferred way to fix the now-broken mockCallbackContext test double (or at minimum lists the specific new methods a hand-patched mock would need)
The rewritten code compiles conceptually against v2 (uses agent.Context correctly in the tool function signature, and updates the mock type)
Does not claim v1 is deprecated, abandoned, or no longer maintained
